question: How many dengue cases will Singapore's NEA report for the epidemiological week ending Saturday 24 October 2026?

calls.reasoning: Recent weekly counts have held between 71 and 87 for six full weeks (E35-40: 87,73,74,82,71,79). E-week 41 had 49 cases by 11am Thursday 16 Oct, with a daily pace of ~10, which projects to ~68-80. Comparing successive cumulative totals shows first-published weekly figures barely get revised. Late October is the tail of the May-Oct peak season, so a mild decline is plausible, while El Niño and three red clusters argue against a sharp drop. Median ~73 with an SD of ~11. No human market found on Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi (harness search plus none known).

calls.reasoning: Anchor: the six completed weeks E35-40 ran 71-87 (mean ~78; latest 79). Late October is the end of Singapore's May-Oct season, so a mild decline is the base expectation. E-week 41 had 49 cases through 11am Friday 16 Oct. Its Sun-Wed daily counts (37) were slightly above E40's 34 for the same days, and E40 went on to finish at 79. So E41 probably lands around 62-75, not a sharp drop. Three red clusters and El Niño warnings support the upper tail. First-published weekly values appear close to final (the change in the cumulative total equalled the new week's count), so the provisional read-time effect is small. No human market found (harness search of Polymarket/Manifold; none known on Kalshi or bookmakers). Median 69.
calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: Run 1 said the 49-case partial count ran to Thursday 16 Oct; Runs 2 and 3 said Friday. 24 Oct 2026 is a Saturday, so 16 Oct is a Friday and Runs 2 and 3 are right. That means only the rest of Friday and Saturday were missing, which weakens Run 1's projection of 68-80. However, Run 3's projection of 60-68 ignores the E40 precedent: E40 also had a low partial count after four days (34) and finished at 79, which suggests late-added reports. E41's Sun-Wed figure (37) is above E40's, so I put E41 at about 62-75. I don't count the partial week as strong evidence of a drop. On revisions, all runs accept that first-published values change little, so the read-time effect is minor. The seasonal decline versus clusters/El Niño question is a judgment call; I lean toward a mild decline. I centre at 69, a little below the plateau. No web retrieval was done on this run.
